utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue, I'd like to deal briefly with one matter. The Defence filed a video-conference link motion on the 30th of September which, if granted, might be able to be combined with another video-conference link scheduled for the end of the month. Considering this possibility, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to expedite its response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This morning I'd like to direct your attention to incident G-6 in Alipasino Polje on 22nd of January, 1994. As part of this incident, there were three shells that exploded; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I'll give you a second here. I see that you're flipping to that section of your report.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to open that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were able to examine the remains of only one of the three impacts because two of the craters were no longer visible when you went to the site to examine them in 2010; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We found traces at Klare Cetkin number 4, in Cetinjska Street number 3, there were no traces remaining and near Rade Koncar, that point of impact was not analysed. It's not in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you would listen to my questions carefully. I'd like to go step by step. One of these craters was not preserved because the shell landed in soil and one of the craters was fully repaved; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The only crater that you were able to physically examine in 2010 was the remains of the crater that landed on Klare Cetkin Street correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This was the crater from the shell that landed on the curb; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, close to the curb.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the time of your visit in 2010, you noticed that this remaining crater was physically altered with part of the curb being repaved in the area of the crater; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a new block was built into the curb. It was not exactly repaved but a new block was made and placed into the curb. If it had been repaved, then it would all have been covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your analysis for the impact on Cetinjska number 3, was based on still images from Barry Hogan's video in 2001 and from other photographs that you obtained from a witness in the Karadzic cases; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we also used the photo documentation made by the crime-scene officer when he was making his on-site investigation, and I believe this street is called Cetinjska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The investigators measured all three craters and one was found to be significantly larger than the other two, specifically one was 4.8 metres long and two of the craters measured less than 180 centimetres in length; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 68 of your report, and this is in -- on page 106 in e-court of the English - you note what you feel to be discrepancies and state: "And police investigators did not use any method to determine the direction available to them, such as, for instance, the central axis method but determined the direction on their estimates." This statement is not accurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. They did nothing to document in their report how they determined it. They only put it in as a written statement that a certain direction is indicated. In crime-scene investigations, that means nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You reviewed the evidence of Mirza Sabljica regarding this event. Did you follow Mr. Sabljica's testimony in this case where he discussed incident G6, and at transcript page 8058, he stated: "We used the usual method. We used the extra central axis method." Did you follow that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I didn't deny that he said it. I just said that it is not documented in their documentation how they did it. And we reviewed their other documentations where all this is properly documented and shown, including, photographs, in the photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you base your Mr. Sabljica's evaluation of Karadzic evidence on what you just heard in court or did you read Mr. Sabljica's statement in the Karadzic case where you further described the methods that he used during this incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must not forget that I was in the courtroom when he was giving evidence in the Karadzic case. And immediately after that, when we showed him the traces on the asphalt from the impact of a shell in Klare Cetkin Street number 4, he also agreed - and you will see that in the transcript - that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- determined the direction correctly. So these two things are contradictory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You haven't fully answered my question. Did you also read his statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recall from the Karadzic case that you were confronted with many instances where you made inaccurate, incorrect, or incomplete representations about the testimony of Mr. Sabljica and other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You repeat many of the same representations in your present report. Did you go back and review Mr. Sabljica's evidence or the testimony of other witnesses after your last testimony to make sure that they were accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We reviewed everything. We followed testimonies and we did not find any reason to find any correction whatsoever in the sense that you indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33117, page 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is your testimony from the Karadzic case regarding incident -- it's part of it regarding incident G-6. The paragraphs are the same so this is in reference to the same paragraph in this report, number 68. Starting at line 19, you were asked: "Q. Ms. Subotic --"

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I don't have the translation of this transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Carefully listen to how it is translated to you now, because there's no B/C/S translation existing. If you need any portion to be reread don't hesitate to ask, but carefully listen do what comes to new your own language. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to start at line 19: "Q. Ms. Subotic, at paragraph 68 - I'd like to move on to paragraph 68 now, which is at page 49 of the English and page 102 of the B/C/S - you -- if we could zoom in on this photo. In paragraph 68, you claim that Mr. Sabljica contradicted himself in his testimony. You state that although Mr. Sabljica initially stated that this -- the shell that made this impact came in from a direction slightly north of west, you say that he later agreed that the direction shown by the measuring tape on this photograph was not properly established. And you repeated this in your testimony at transcript page 38262. Now, you were present when Mr. Sabljica testified so you must know that Mr. Sabljica, in fact, made it very clear that it was improper to establish direction of fire from a photograph and that this is not what they did at the time, and that's at transcript page 7829 -7830 and when he was asked to draw the traces on this photo, he said: "'Well, that's what we can see in the photo at least.' "And that's T.7847 and D755. And when he was asked to mark tracts on another photo of this crater he said: 'Yes, I will, but I have to stress again that a photo is not really the appropriate way to determine these things but here it is.' "That's T.7849 and D756. "So when you claim in your report that Mr. Sabljica agreed that the direction showed by this measuring tape was properly established you're essentially misrepresenting his evidence because he made it quite clear that could you not properly establish anything on the basis of a photograph; right?" Your answer: "Mr. Sabljica, in my view, agreed with us and said that this is the fact that traces are well determined on the asphalt and that he established the trajectory of the shell correctly." Do you maintain this view?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica agreed with the direction that we showed him, and he said that it was properly determined based on the photograph. I agree with Mr. Sabljica that it is far better to do it on the spot and immediately after the critical event. It is much better to analyse it and determine it on location. Then you are likely to get correct results. However, Mr. Sabljica saw perfectly well that the traces we found many years later are more than 3 metres away from the curb and it could no way be an 82-millimetre shell. That's one. And two, he agreed with what we determined as a direction is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you saying that that Mr. Sabljica actually agreed with you about a photograph being a proper way of determining direction of fire? If you could please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And he was not asked that. He was asked whether it was correct that we properly marked the traces as they were on the asphalt and if it is true that the measuring tape that was placed across the traces indicated the correct direction. That's what he agreed with.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33188.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is Mr. Sabljica's Karadzic testimony that was referenced in my last question to you. At transcript page 7829, starting at line 17, Mr. Sabljica was asked: "Q. Do you agree that there is a certain perspective here in view of the distance from which the photograph was taken? "A. You mean in terms of approach to photography? Yes, there is a perspective. "Q. Do we agree that perspective makes it more difficult to establish direction? "A. I agree, but a direction is not established based on photographs; that's also a very important fact. We did not use photographs to determine directions, we used exact methods on the site, that is to say" -- And if we could have the next page. "... firm traces on surfaces not photographs. Working on photographs and drawing on photographs can give you completely different results." You were present when Mr. Sabljica said this; correct.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Moving on: "If we look at paragraph 68 of your report and again at paragraph 75, you state: "Mirza Sabljica agreed that according to the map the line extending from number 4 Klare Cetkin Street to the institute for the blind is due south-west." The map that you are referring to is the map he marked during his Karadzic testimony, which was Exhibit D746 in that case. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D01413, page 93. During Mr. Sabljica's Karadzic testimony, on this map, which is before you, at page 7805, line 8, Mr. Sabljica was asked: "Q. But you do know what streets these were. Is that the 8 symbol that we see there at the eastern part, the eastern 8 symbol, the Klare Cetkin Street and Bosanska Street? "A. Well, it's about here." - there's a notion [sic] that he indicated - "I can't quite mark the area -- the point of impact where these shells fell, but I'll just indicate the general area." At line 20 on this same page, the question was posed by

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Could you now please indicate, with numbers 1, 2, and 3, the location where they landed?" Mr. Sabljica answered: "Well, I really can't do that. As I told you a minute ago, it's a large area and it's built up. There are a lot of buildings there. You know what Alipasin Polje looked like. It's difficult to do that." Could the Prosecution please have the next page. And if we go down towards line 24 on this page, Judge Kwon even commented during this discussion: "The quality maybe is not very well, Mr. Karadzic. I think it is a scanned copy from the copy again." Since you were present during this testimony, you were aware that when Mr. Sabljica was asked to make markings on this map which Judge Kwon commented on being a of poor quality, he continuously said that he could not mark on the map without difficulty. That is what happened.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are we talking about the map that is shown on figure 63 in our report? I don't have now with me the photograph that was shown to Mr. Sabljica, and it's difficult for me to remember two and a half years later what it looked like. I don't know which picture was shown him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you acknowledge that you witnessed the testimony that I've just read to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot not accept it because I was there during his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll ask you a more broad question because there are many other instances in your report where you do not provide full explanations or context related to the use of maps or photos with witnesses, such as discussions of poor qualities of maps or photos, or the fact that witnesses either did not agree or were -- it was difficult for them to mark on a certain photo used by Mr. Karadzic. You accept that you don't provide full context for that testimony in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in everyone citation the context is cited very precisely. If you claim different, then I would like you to show me instance by instance. But I would like your leave for me to give you a full answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to go through many instances today. And I continue on. In paragraph 68 of your shelling report, which is 1D05498, you indicate that Captain Verdy determined the direction of fire for two of the shells as 4200 mills and 4250 mills which correspond to 236 degrees and 239 degrees with a margin of error of plus or minus 5 degrees. The direction of fire that you appear to have estimated based on the materials available to you were 238 degrees and 240 degrees. I'm locating that in paragraphs 68 and 70 of your report. Your estimates are within the margin of error of those determined by Captain Verdy; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It only means that our assessment was sound. For precision's sake, I would kindly ask that we rely on professional jargon. It is not mills. The unit is called 1.000th part which is different from a mill. Just so that nobody would later on try to convert the mills into degrees and then declare this a mistake. That unit is used in artillery and it is called the thousandth part it is determined by the 360 degrees in a circle which in one system that is used, amounts to 6.000th units whereas in the western system, the number of thousandths is 6.400.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I asked you a very simple question. Your determinations of 238 degrees and 240 degrees is within the margins of error that Captain Verdy determined; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you followed, I said that our assessment was sound. They were made -- that assessment was made in Klare Cetkin Street number 4 based on material evidence rather than photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Ms. Subotic, I take it that you consider your own estimates to be sound. But the question was a different one, whether your estimate stayed within a margin of error what was established by Mr. Sabljica. Is it within those margins of error, or is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Verdy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Verdy --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Captain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise. Is it or is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The values we came up with are extremely close to his.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes that's an answer to the question. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the report of Captain Verdy - admitted as D178 - Captain Verdy indicates that the direction of fire that impacted number 4 Klare Cetkin Street where five individuals were killed is 4200 mills, or 236 degrees, and for the shell that impacted number 3 Cetinjska Street, is 4250 mills, or 239 degrees correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In figure 62 of your report, at page 114, you inverse the measurements taken by Captain Verdy in his UNPROFOR report and indicate that the direction of fire for the shell that impacted on Klare Cetkin Street was 239 degrees and the one on Cetinjska Street was 236 degrees. You did this; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did it based on the material evidence following the explosion of the mine at the site of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At paragraph 71 of your report, pages 112 to 113, you claim that Captain Verdy made a mistake when he recorded the direction of fire of the two shells and that he inverted the measurements of the two craters. Without inverting the direction of fire that you did, the direction of fire for the two shells would not converge but actually they would diverge; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But they cannot remain the same because of the traces left by the shells on asphalt when they impacted. Each shell leave a distinct mark based on the direction of trajectory and based on that, we concluded that without any doubt Captain Verdy made his measurements based on the bearings found on some photographs that were actually taken in mistake, that they were not the accurate photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33189.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is an annotated map that you saw during your last time here. On this map, there are two black lines representing the direction of fire of 239 and 236 degrees corresponding to Captain Verdy's measurements. There are also two lightly shaded yellow cones which overlap and form a darker yellow shaded area. Do you agree that the possible directions of fire calculated by Captain Verdy would fall within the yellow ranges indicated on this map, based on plus or minus 5 margin of error that he determined?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your report, you assume - and I put to you without any support - that these two rounds came from the same mortar. Now even assuming that this is true, these rounds would have come from a mortar in the darker yellow shaded area, correct, where the two cones overlap?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is professionally impermissible for me to allow you such comments. In the course of this entire procedure, which has taken between 15 and 20 years now, there has been no investigator who would agree that -- who would not agree that the shells were fired from one and the same tube. We have technical facts that -- to support that thesis and all of the shells landed within only one possible deviation degree per distance which is something that would be impossible to do if there were more tubes than one. Of course there must be certain corrections between two shells in order to have them hit Klare Cetkin and Cetinjska Street in terms of direction. Expert Higgs agrees with us that corrections were made in terms of distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... ma'am, my question was much more simple and I would appreciate if you would answer it. If -- the two shots were fired from the same mortar, that mortar would fall into the darker yellow shaded area on what we see before us; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kindly explain to me where you think that would -- that would be the case. I don't see the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you don't see the point -- at transcript page 39267, you indicated that Captain Verdy's determination of direction of fire conflicted with the direction of fire determined by the CSB investigators who said that the shells came from the direction of the Nedzarici school for the blind. I would kindly ask that you be handed an a pen, and I'm going to ask you to mark this image before us based on your own personal knowledge, if you could please mark the location of the Nedzarici school for the blind with an X. Not based on anything -- aside, ma'am, from your own personal knowledge. I believe you've indicated that you've gone to this location.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I visited all of the locations. There's no problem there. But they need to be put back on the map. It should be around here, somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't see any marking. Could the usher assist. Apparently there's some technical problem in the marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can come back to it quickly later today then. Just have her mark on that quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we perhaps already -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be repaired over the break most likely, but could we already with the assistance of the usher, can we have the witness indicate where the witness thinks the school for the blind is by using the cursor. Could you assist, Ms. Subotic, you see the arrow which is the cursor? Could you give instructions so as to move it to where the school of the blind is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you say to the left, up, down? Could you please assist the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be to the right. Right. Not left. A bit more up. To the right. Just behind the red line on the right-hand side. To the right. Down. Right. Slowly. Right, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A bit up. There. More or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness points at a -- one second. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be there, approximately. As far as I recall it on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness points at a place which is to the right of where a road is marked 18 E 762052 to the right of that and a little bit up, just south -- just a little bit below where the road is called Stupsko Brdo but still within the red dotted line. As a matter of fact, the pointer exactly at a road which is parallel to Stupsko Brdo just parallel, just below where that can be read just a bit north of a complex of what seems to be buildings, that is, black small blocks. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, this is --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps even a bit higher up north, because the bearing of the home for the blind is 266, so almost clear west as opposed to -- compared to the place of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you again look at the cursor and give directions. Is it at the right place now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's say it is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not let's say, but is it correct, as far as your recollection goes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I recall, it is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can make a screen shot, including the cursor. Madam Registrar, could you take care that a screen shot is made. It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I must say that my technical knowledge, I think it should be uploaded first and then once the screen shot has ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar tells me that this is sufficient for having it tendered into evidence. Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7553, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, the area that you've indicated, I put to you, is actually much further to the north than the actual school for the blind, and you have indicated an incorrect location.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so. Since where we see the figures 8s, that is the place of the incident. The institute for the blind has the bearing of 266 compared to the buildings we considered. So we can take it as being the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You measured that 266? Is that your determination that it's 266 degrees as a bearing from the location of the incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We took it off Google Earth. If you followed Mr. Sabljica's transcript, he agreed with it in his testimony in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think you're aware that we dispute that. I'd like to discuss more incidents with you here. Moving on in your report, you comment upon four shellings in the area of Dobrinja between 1993 and 1995. These are the explosions on 1 June 1993, incident G-4; 4 February 1994, incident G-7; and two unscheduled incidents on 12 July 1993 and 18 June 1995, both at water distribution points? On all of the occasions, the explosions were caused by mortar impacts; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Focussing on the shelling of the football match on 1 June 1993, scheduled incident G-4, you conclude that the direction of fire for this incident was in the south-easterly direction; I'd refer you to paragraph 41 of your report. On this trajectory, the furthest distance the shell could have been fired from ABiH territory was 200 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why do you think it is the furthest distance? The separation lines were quite close there, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In figure 30 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, please listen to my question carefully again. On the trajectory that you claim, the furthest distance the shell could have been fired from ABiH territory was 200 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. According to the map provided by Ismet Hadzic where he marked the separation lines, we could see that the distance to the trenches was 270 metres rather than 200. We provided that in figure 36.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33117, e-court page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is your past testimony in the Karadzic case. At transcript page 20, you were asked: "Q. Well, and the trajectory you concluded was the south-easterly trajectory. So I'm saying that if it was fired from this trajectory, from ABiH territory, the furthest distance it could have been fired from is 200 metres from the incident. Are we agreed on that?" Your answer was: "Yes." That was your previous answer; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That information was specified by different witnesses. We checked it and compared it to the map and came up with 270 rather than 200. I think it to be a more precise piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A distance of 200 to 250 metres would be on or near the confrontation line; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are talking here about the positions close to the separation lines, much as we discussed the position of 400 metres, which was the closest one, and sheltered when viewing from the separation line. As you could probably notice in the captions above and below the photograph in paragraph 45. It is the closest point possible to the existing positions at the confrontation lines. Or, rather, the -- to the border cases possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you visited this location in 2010, the craters were born down from vehicle and foot traffic along with erosion over time; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We attached photographs showing what they looked like precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see we're at the time for a break. I was just about to go into a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are at the time for a break. Ms. Subotic, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was informed that the screen shot didn't work either, so perhaps the marking should be briefly now be done by marking it on the screen because I do understand that the problem that existed earlier has now been fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And I believe up on the screen is 65 ter 33189, unmarked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can do it right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you stay with the witness because the screen shot didn't work and, therefore, we'll -- Mr. Weber will invite the witness to mark again where the school for the blind is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, I believe we've resolved our technical difficulties. If could you please on the image that's before you mark an X at the location where you believe the Nedzarici school for the blind is located.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 33189 as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think what we should do is to vacate the number that was assigned earlier because the screen shot didn't work and that, Madam Registrar, under the same number now we'll decide on admission of this map marked by the witness. That would ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7553, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7553 is now the map, and I think you gave the number a second ago, Mr. Weber. That is -- let me see, 33189 as now marked by the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and, of course, that's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As you indicated in your past testimony, you are aware that there are different maps that use different grid systems; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you are trying to say with this "different grid systems." I know there are different maps but I don't understand what you mean by different grid systems. Maps are more or less with the same grid systems, only the scales differ between maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your past testimony at transcript page 38410, you stated: "As far as I know, there are two systems. We checked both and we could not find the grid references that would correspond with the location of the parking lot." Next question was: "And what's the basis for your conclusion that there are only two grid systems in the world?" Your answer was: "I am aware of two grid systems which depend on the number of figures which you read when you do the analysis." You are aware that there are different grid systems; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, that's what you mean. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to figure 30 and footnote 131 on e-court page 66 of your report, you plotted the grid co-ordinate provided by Captain Houdet on a series 903 map; correct? If you could please particularly check footnote 131?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, the footnote was? I was looking for the picture that I had forgotten. I'm sure not sure I heard the number of the footnote.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a very familiar map to this Chamber. It is, for the record, included on multiple occasions in the Sarajevo map book as the base map, Exhibit P3. My question to you, did you realise when you were doing your report that the scale for the series 903 map is 1 to 12.500?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I saw that. I don't remember. I don't remember that detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the -- could we have that map on our screen because I see a map black-and-white version that mention made of a green circle but in black and white, green is not easy to detect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is 1D5498.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm actually moving on to another exhibit to look at another map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, nevertheless, I would like to have a look at what you have drawn our attention to on figure 30. I just wanted to have a brief look at that. And that's -- I don't have the -- it's in the English version, it's page 66 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Picture 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that's not an e-court number perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 62 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Could we enlarge the map. I think we had the map -- we had the map a second ago. This is 26. Could we move onto --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe it was e-court page 66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's hard copy page 66 as well. Yes. Could we zoom in on the map itself. Yes, now I see the green circle. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P644 for the witness. And if we could please go to page 9 of the English original and page 8 of the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is Captain Houdet's report which is attached as Annex A to the 7 July 1993 UN investigation report with two other documents as part of that annex. Did you review the full UN investigation report for this incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We'll go through some additional materials in a second. While we're on it, you're aware that Captain Houdet's report refers to two craters; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the top of Captain Houdet's report, we see the grid reference and then "map 1/50.000 Sarajevo, sheet 27821, series M709." Captain Houdet used a different series map with a different scale than the one in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you not find a series M709 map or a grid map with a 1 to 50.000 scale when you were doing your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We provided the map that we had at our disposal, the only one we were able to find.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page of the original only of this exhibit. In the English, is the original. And if we could make this the full screen, please, and if we could please rotate it. There we go. Ooh.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the map attached to Captain Houdet's report which is part of the same annex. In the upper right-hand corner, you see the scale 1 to 50.000; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please zoom -- actually, there should be fine. Do you see the numerical references for the longitude and latitude grid lines, the -- they appear across the middle of the document on the grid lines, running horizontally, and they're a little bit off to the left of centre, running vertically on the grid lines? You see those; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 84, 85, et cetera. That's what you mean. Those are the numbers we see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you see the location marked at the point of impact on this map where the two lines representing the direction of fire converge from the south-east? The top line runs through the number 55 on its way towards Dobrinja. The lower line runs through the number 54 on its way to Dobrinja from the south-east.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot see 55 to be honest, but I see a line -- oh, yes, I see it here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The point of impact is marked approximately in the centre and a little bit to the left, in the grid corresponding to 87 on the horizontal axis and 56 on the vertical axis; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 87 on the vertical axis ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On the horizontal axis.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's very difficult to read these numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. The location of the point of impact on this map does not correspond to the location you marked on a completely different series map; correct? That's what we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If the witness should say something about the difference between two maps she should first be able to find the point of impact as shown in this map. Perhaps we can zoom in on the upper left-hand corner of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But still such that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, if you could please draw your attention to the screen. You can see where the point of impact is on -- before us; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just read the co-ordinates given in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you found the point of impact? That's the question, as plotted on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The way it is drawn into this map, yes. But I cannot read, I cannot find the numbers given by Captain Verdy [as interpreted] on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I perhaps briefly assist you. Do you see the numbers which are to the bottom left. It says -- close to the cursor, it says 84, then next line is 85, then 86, 87, 88, 89. And if you now from 89 move up, you see the first -- the first line is 54, the second is 55, the third is 56. And then the following is 57. Have you find [sic] your -- these numbers on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The location of the point of impact on this map does not correspond to the location that you marked on the different series map; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent I can find my way around this map that I'd never seen before, let's say that it's correct, with the proviso that in this report it says that both shells fell on macadam surface within this playground and this residential building, this is not indicated. In any case, we determined it was 200 metres from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- from the grounds where a football match was played.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, we know what your report says. If you could please focus on the questions and answer the questions only and we'll move along. I'd like to turn your attention to the video from the local media correspond and related to this incident which was filmed after the shelling on 1 June 1993. You have seen part of it during your direct examination. At this time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could we first establish whether the witness agrees? Because that was your question because she marked the point of impact at a location different from the one we saw on the map used at the time as part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, did you hear His Honour's comment?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can only check in the afternoon what the difference is between this map and the map that we used and what the influence is, if any, of this map on our conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if I look at this map, it looks as if the point of impact as plotted in the report made at the time is just below, south of the main road leading to Lukavica, whereas the centre of the green circle which you plotted as the point of impact is north of that road, above that road. Would you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the question was whether you plotted it at a different place as was done at the time in this report made contemporaneously.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now my question - a very short question - would be: You said I have never seen that report but that map was part of a report at the time. Does that mean that did you not look at that report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I reviewed everything that was available to me from this package relating to this incident, and all of that is cited in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that map was part of the report which you said a map you had never seen before and was not available to you. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's well understood. I did not see it before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Though being part of the report which was made at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very often we received only partial documents, documents that were not complete and related to different reports of different incidents. Some things came to us in a complete package; others didn't. And that's nothing unusual in our job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you make mention of that in your report, that you did not have access to the full information from the report which you referred to in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you have probably seen, in some incidents, we did indicate that something was missing; in others, we did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you do it in this instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe in this specific incident we did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to now play 65 ter 33095A. For the record there's been a provisional exhibit number reserved for it which is I believe is D1250. But the parties have to work out the agreed full timing of the clip. It is the local video footage after the shelling on 1 June 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You play which part?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We're going to -- if I could just have two seconds into the -- actually, I'm going to play the first ten seconds of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you just repeat the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is 33095A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We are paused at 11 seconds -- 11 and a half seconds into the video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The image on the screen is similar to the images that you place in your report from this video; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the upper left corner of this image that is now on the screen, you agree that one of the goals is visible between the red and blue cars correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this part of the video, you cannot see the second goal; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You also do not see a second row of cars; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. If there is a second row of cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please play the video another six seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please play another two seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There we go. We are now paused at 19.3 seconds into the video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see a row of cars. There's no blue car in this row. And the cars appear to be positioned differently; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In front of the second car from the left, you see another football goal there; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, which second car? You mean the red car, the second red car or white and then red? I can't see very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm referring you to the second red car from the left. If you focus immediately in -- towards us from that car where the passenger door would be. There's a second goal there; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the opposite side. I'm sorry, the picture is unclear. I could not say that it's the second goal, but if we could focus better maybe, so we can distinguish things more clearly, maybe I can agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could back up two seconds on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I'm going to play it for four seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you able to see the second goal in front of the car?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is something in front of the car, but I cannot seriously conclude, unlike with the previous picture, that it is that. It seems to me too close to the car, or maybe that's the way this video is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You agree that we're looking at another row of cars from the direction of the goal at the opposite end of the pitch; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not going to tender at this time, pending agreement with the Defence as to what should be included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the number has been reserved already and you would like to add the first 20-plus 03 seconds of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that the Defence showed two portions of the video one from before what we see on the screen and one from after what we saw on the screen so if we could -- I think what we'll agree to is one full segment that includes images that were shown just now and images that were shown after by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you started at 0 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what was shown before that is that minus or.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was starting at the same time code.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. I see that you mean the part shown by the Defence was a portion which precedes what you have drawn our attention to now. Please proceed. I still have another small question. If we look at figure 30, Witness, who did plot the numbers 8739 and 5653 and the green circle? Who did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We drew that to put in the co-ordinates and indicate the place and the co-ordinates given by Captain Verdy in the basic report on the map that we cited below.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now are those grid references given on that map? I mean, in general? Which enabled you to plot it as you did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are the grid references cited in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you. I asked you where you plotted those grid references, whether they are found such a grid system on the map on which you plotted them and drew a green circle? Or did you implant from any other map, the grid references?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, those are the co-ordinates, the grid references that correspond to the red circle. And read from this map where they are drawn. The source of these numbers is in the report.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last thing she said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last thing you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The numeric source of these co-ordinates is in the report of Captain Boudet [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was from where did you take the grid references in general. Did you take them from the map on which you then finally plotted the grid references as given by Verdy, or did you take them from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry to interrupt. I believe on this incident it is Captain Houdet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Houdet. I'm mixing up all the French names, and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You took them from this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The numbers were taken from the report numerically speaking. He provided the co-ordinates of the incident. On this map, according to its scale, the co-ordinates are marked in green in the green circle. I don't know how better to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, in order to plot something on a map, if you have certain numbers, you need to know what grid system is used in the map which you mark. My question is whether the grid system, whether you took that from the map you used or did you take it from anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The co-ordinates shown in the report, in terms of numbers, were found on the map we used and marked in a red circle. They were numerically identified as to be able to establish a link with the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your discussion of the G-4 shelling, you criticise Richard Higgs for agreeing with Captain Houdet's conclusion as to range and at the end of paragraph 42 of your report, you indicate that Mr. Higgs's conclusion is a sign of bias. From your past testimony, you are aware that Expert Higgs performed an independent analysis related to the crater; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I'm familiar with that, and we cite his analysis. He made use of the same analysis of the crater that we did. He concluded that there was no reason to analyse further because he saw it only in 2001, much after it had happened. He could see two traces in the field where, in 1995, there were none.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I think he should have taken all of that into account and not only the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please stay focussed on my questions, and I'm going to go through it as to what happened the last time you were asked about this. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33117 for the witness. And if we could please go to page 23. This is your past testimony in the Karadzic case where you were discussing paragraph 42 of your report. Starting at line 3, you were asked: "Q. Certainly I can do that. Let me ask it this way. Mr. Higgs in his Galic testimony concluded when he looked at the crater that it must have come in at an angle of between -- an angle of descent of between 50 and 70 degrees. So my question for you is: If he was correct and, in fact, the maximum angle of descent was 70 degree, it's true, is it not, that the mortar would have to have been fired from the SRK side of the confrontation line? Do you agree with that? "A. I will agree with you if I look at the tables because I really don't know this by heart, the angles of descent and whether we provided them in this document or not. I have to have a look at the angles. I really don't know the tables off the top of my head." Do you stand by this testimony.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. I really don't know the tables by heart, and please don't expect me to. I don't know all the numerical parts off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your report in this case is dated April 2014, after this testimony. When you completed this report for this case, you were aware of Mr. Higgs's conclusion that, based on what he looked at at the crater, that the angle of descent was between 50 to 70 degrees; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It was his conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours -- oh, I see it was just corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You do not mention Mr. Higgs's conclusion on the angle of descent being between 50 and 70 degrees in your Mladic report, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. We mentioned Witness John Hamill who said that it was 65 degrees. We agree that it was the approximate angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You also do not include Mr. Higgs's testimony on 4 November 2013 in this case - and I'm referring to transcript page 18762 - where you indicated that he looked at the crater and the angle of descent based on his personal observations using the range tables gave him a minimum range of 300 metres. You don't reference that in your report either; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P7549, page 54 of the B/C/S and page 80 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. These are the 82-millimetre mortar tables again. First let's determine the mills that correspond to the maximum angle of descent of 70 degrees I'm going to do this based on the 1 to 6.000 mills calculation. If I could direct your attention to the fourth column to the left, there is a number 70 under the column for degrees. And then one column over to the right, it states 1166.67. 70 degrees corresponds to 11166.67 mills; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of thousandths, not of mills.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You do realise that the tables do refer to mills; correct and I understand it's on a 1 to 6.000 calculation. If we could move on to page 12 of both versions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, we find both; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So whether this table refers to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. I was -- we find here, if I understand well, a translation of both western, which if I understand well, is 1 to 6400, and eastern, that is 1 to 6.000 mills, into degrees. That's what we find here. So to say that -- to say that it's 1 on a 6.000 calculation, that is true for those columns where it says at the top: 1-6.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think we're both understood. Could the Prosecution please go to page 12 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness would like to add something. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a moment ago what it was. Yes, just a while ago, I tried to distinguish between mills and thousandths because it is an artillery aspect in use. All tables are more or less provided in thousandths as well as all of the sighting devices which use that unit. We have a full circle of 360 degrees, in one system it equals 6.000s, in the other 6.400 thousandths it is may not be directly related to mills --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a matter of terminology I -- from what I understood from the evidence, that what you call thousandths are often referred to as mills in the eastern system, whereas the 1 to 6400 is often referred to as the mills in the western system, or the mills, if I -- and I think that is clear in table 8a where the conversion of degrees into thousands, thousands which are here including both 1 to 6.000 and 1 to 6400. I think there's no disagreement on what the table tells us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 12 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the table for the 82-millimetre M74 on zero charge. Directing your attention to column 9, if you could go down in that column. Do you see the listing for 1149 right below the zero on the page?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Going over to the far left column this angle of descent, which is roughly around 69 degrees, would correspond to range of 325 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The line above corresponds to a range of 300 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I appreciate it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you said for the 325 you have around 69 degrees. What I see for 325 is 67 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- degrees and for the one further up, 69 degrees --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, actually, I think that's the firing angle. Not necessarily the angle of descent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with you. If we look at 9. Let's have a look at 9. 9 is the angle of descent. And that is apparently in mills again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the question is what kind of mills?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's all 1 to 6.000 because that is found in columns 3 and 4, where degrees that the conversion of the mills in degrees stems from -- from the 1 to 6.000 type of mill and therefore you say it's reasonable to expect that the angle of descent equally uses the same mills rather than the other system. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And on the previous page that we just looked at we see that 69 degrees is a little bit -- is one one thousandths above this. It 1150 thousandths in the 1 to 6.000 scale. That's where I'm getting the information from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: An angle of descent of 70 degrees would correlate to a range of around 300 to 325 metres; correct.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to head into a new incident. I can keep on going. I'll just keep going for a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have five minutes left. If you'd rather than do it one stretch then perhaps it would be better to take the break now --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- rather than to interrupt it halfway. Ms. Subotic, we'll take another break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, turning your attention to incident G-7, the shelling of a queue for humanitarian assistance in Dobrinja on 4 February 1994, the craters had changed by the time of your visit in 2010. One of the areas on the playground was paved over, and the area where all of the people were lined up still had damage on the building but the crater was no longer there; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: One of your criticisms - and I'm referring to paragraph 83 of your report - is that a sketch of the scene in the investigation file does not have north marked correctly on it. You indicate that it has an error of 60 degrees and then you wrote: "As a consequence of this error in determining the north, the incoming trajectory was also determined erroneously." At the end of the paragraph, however, you write: "At first sight, the error made in marking the north on the sketch of the scene may appear accidental and immaterial but the final conclusion must be reserved until after we have analysed the manner in which the incoming trajectory of the shells was determined and after we have verified whether this error in determining the north has affected the conclusion about the incoming direction of the shell." If the sketch was not used in the process of determining the incoming trajectory of the shells, then any error in marking the direction of north on the sketch would be immaterial; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P867, which is the investigative file for this incident, and could we please go to English page 12 and B/C/S page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the forensic report for incident G-7 which tells you how the direction was determined, and a little further down in -- under item 4, the report says: "Incoming direction of the mortar shell was determined with magnetic compass ..." You do not mention this fact in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. In this report we mention twice this type of determining direction, and we dispute it based on technical aspects or results of the shell at the place of impact and we also dispute it on the basis of a map and its position. The map has a large scale, and as can be seen from the photograph, it was placed without any reference points. In that case you can position it whichever you want compared to a compass --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I think you may have seen that in the report but I don't know why you fail to mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to go through what you didn't cite in the report. You are mentioning other items. If, over the next break, you could just tell me where you refer to this quote from the report that we have on the screen that would be appreciated. Could the Prosecution please have page 32 of the B/C/S version only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can the witness have the quote on the screen printed out for her because --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because to ask her where to find it's mainly about the magnetic compass being used for the determination. Witness, you are invited to -- during the next break to find in your report where you refer to determining the incoming direction of the mortar shell with a magnetic compass and I think the emphasis is on --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may assist, Your Honour, it's on figure 77.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Figure 77.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it already. It is the second paragraph following figure 75, where this type of determination is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you've --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was trying to specifically refer to the forensic report. We see that she does refer to this photo which is where I'm going next.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a photo from the photo file. This is the photo that you do refer to and it shows that the magnetic compass pointed and pointed to the north, correct? Along with the incoming trajectory of one of the shells? And maybe to assist the witness, we can zoom in on the compass.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in your opinion, what can we see on the compass? The north? I have no objection to it being so. But it doesn't determine the incoming trajectory and there is no reference point on the basis of which the trajectory could be determined in that way. The direction of north is shown on a compass always the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you testified about this in the Karadzic case, you claim that the individual who drew the sketch, Witness KDZ-166, agreed with you. You said: "Due to this error of 60 degrees, they drew erroneous conclusions about the direction from which the shells had arrived. I think that KDZ-166, the witness agreed with this when we presented to him the situation as depicted here." And this is at transcript page 38271 in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, ma'am --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I thought that was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now ma'am -- you were also confronted with the language that KDZ-166 had actually used which was at transcript page 8297 of the Karadzic trial where the witness was asked: "Now we have a new northerly direction so if you change it from 90 degrees to some 30 or 40 degrees, does that affect the direction from which the shell came? " The witness answered: "No, it doesn't. I did not plot the direction onto my sketch from which the shell came because that part of the work, that is, to establish the direction, was done by ballistics experts." In your present report in this case, you then don't make reference to this fact, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we said, it is irrelevant whether he determined the incoming trajectory or not. On the sketch --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- showing the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Sabljica who is one of the ballistics expert who investigated the scene was also asked about this and said the sketch was irrelevant to determining direction of fire. The reasons he gave was: "Because what we did in our investigations had to do with the actual situation and the actual trace evidence found at the site." This is the Karadzic transcript, page 7800. You also leave this part of Mr. Sabljica's testimony out for this incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. As you just read, we stated here that we wanted to determine whether it has any importance that the sketch was drawn the way it was drawn, whether it is -- it somehow influenced the conclusions. We cited all the analyses we made of the material evidence and on the basis of which we determined the incoming trajectory. It was very close to what the sketch shows. But you know perfectly well, you have seen it. We made all our conclusions based on the material traces that were on the scene and the material evidence in keeping with the rules of the profession and science based on the documents that the investigators made the next day, which does not detract from their relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I get that's kind of your standard answer today. But what I'd like to specifically ask you is there's nothing in the investigative file or anywhere else indicating that the sketch was actually used to determine the incoming trajectory; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Another theory you have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, one short question. Does the witness still have to try to find the use of the compass or were you just wrong in saying that -- in suggesting that it was not in her report. Because I think in the footnote it clearly states - footnote 361 - where it is taken from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't see reference to the report that I referred to in the footnotes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Footnote 361. Close to the photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I see. I see. The photo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... no, but it also states where the photo is taken from, isn't it? Security service centre photo documentation number 3 -- 234. That's the footnote related to this picture in which the use of a compass is shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand what Your Honour is saying. I'm not going to persist on it, however, what I was asking was about is the report which is a different document than this photo that's cited there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But the witness has explained at least that she even has shown in her report how a compass was used in this context in order to determine the direction of the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Another theory that you have is that four shells landed in the immediate area of the humanitarian line, not three, but that the investigators covered up - and I'm referring to your report paragraph 81 - the fourth shell because it could shot from come from VRS positions; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, no, it's not right. It says here that this shell provides exclusive evidence that such fire could not have come from that direction. That is to say, it rules out the possibility that this fire came in from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. I understood you to be asking something different. In fact, that's how I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 80, you write: "The photo file contains a shot showing the damage to the edge of the footpath which could not have been caused by a shell exploding on the footpath but only from the shrapnel of a shell that exploded in the playground." And then you refer to a figure of your report. I'd like to look at the original photo. Could we please Exhibit P867, page 24 of the B/C/S version only. And if the witness could be provided with assistance in terms of a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, it's figure 67 from the report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the picture taken from the same material we are looking at right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I wanted to start with the fresh image here. Could you please trace with a pen what you consider to be the shrapnel damage that could not have been caused by the shell that hit the footpath.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This damage is also marked in our report. I will now mark it again here. As can be seen, this damage is at 90 degrees relative to the edge of the curb and since the shell came in from the right upper corner towards symbol 1, this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- what is called in artillery a dead angle where shrapnel cannot arrive from the shell that exploded where the number 1 is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the marked image into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The marked image receives exhibit number P7554, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter 1D5498. English page 136 and B/C/S page 132.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention to figures 74 and 75 which look to be both visible in the English version. Here you appear to be essentially saying that the pattern damage on the right-hand wall in the alcove of the apartment building could not have occurred if the shell came in from SRK positions. In figure 74, you have what appears to be a wing pattern of shell fragments that is empty towards the front in the direction of the part of the wall. My first question to you is: These are two-dimensional images that depict the area from above; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
