utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In reality, if we looked at the top image, for example, figure 74, from a horizontal perspective, showing the incoming angle of descent, the shrapnel of the mortar would disperse in 360 degrees and go outward toward the building striking the area under number 3; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, but I don't think that's quite correct. First of all, what do we call the area under number 3? What is that? Mihajlo Pupin Street number 3? Is that what you're trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just referring to it just because it's in the diagram. Let me put it another way; if the mortar would be entering at a downward angle of 45 degrees or more, there would also be fragments that would project straight out in front of the shell; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A shell cannot fall under 45 degrees or less. A minimal angle of descent for a 120-millimetre shell is 52 or 55 degrees. There is no such thing as 45 degrees or less. That does not exist. Mortar cannot hit at such an angle. It doesn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was saying 45 degrees or more so if -- if a mortar fell at an angle of descent of greater than 45 degrees, there would be fragments that would project straight out in front of the shell; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But very little, in a very small amount. If you look at the photographs which --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- depict a real picture you will see that it's not as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... well, I would dispute that and the Chamber has that evidence. I want to keep on moving along. If you could please listen to my questions. In paragraph 97 of your Markale report, you say: "It is well-known that the stabiliser penetrates the ground when it is fired with charge 3 or a higher charge. When a mortar shell is fired with charge 1 or charge 2, the stabiliser falls in the immediate vicinity of the crater or it is propelled back along the approximate trajectory of the shell." In this instance with respect to the shell that hit near the building, you agree the 120-millimetre stabiliser was fully embedded in the crater on the asphalt surface; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On figure 68, we see a stabiliser that fell in Mihajlo Pupin Street number 3 and it not fully embedded. On the contrary. It is lying on the surface with deformations that show that during its descent it changed positions, which means it had prior landing on a different surface and that's one of the reasons why we did not accept that the real incoming trajectory was properly determined using compass.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that's taken from the pictures made by the investigators marked by 7. That's the stabiliser we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You agree that one of the mortar shells were embedded on this instance; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one that fell on the footpath.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's focus on that one, and I'm sorry if I added to that confusion there. And as you acknowledged in the Karadzic case, according to the firing tables for 120-millimetre mortars, this would indicate a minimum firing distance of 600 metres for this shell, the one that was embedded; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is according to the firing tables, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You make some other comments in paragraph 88 of your shelling report about the images of the embedded stabiliser. You indicate that the embedded stabiliser was at almost a vertical angle but the marks on the asphalt do not indicate that the shell was fired with the maximum elevation. In other words, this means that, at the time of the explosion and as the stabiliser penetrated into the soil, its position changed. First of all, you -- the fact is that this was looked at as part of the investigation and the report drafted by Mr. Sabljica, who personally inspected the site specifically, stated that this embedded tail-fin was "facing east." Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether what he saw is accurate and whether what he wrote was accurate. I don't want to go into that. I know the way the fins are turned has absolutely no technical relation to where the projectile came from. The link only exists and it is correct if the descent and the position of the stabiliser coincides with the direction determined based on the traces on the asphalt according to the central axis method. If these two directions coincide that's the only situation where you can determine incoming trajectory based on the position of the stabiliser. The only things mentioned there are absolutely unacceptable for the reasons that are explained in detail in this report. If you wish me to, I can repeat them for the umpteenth time but it depends on a large number of technical parameters that have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- all be present for this to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I want to now discuss with you incident G-5 on the 12th of July, 1993 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you move to another incident --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- I have one question for the witness. Can we have on the screen again, P7554, the photograph of the footpath where you indicated by a circle the impact of a shrapnel. I can already put my question. It will come up soon. How did you determine that this is the place where a shrapnel penetrated the ground? When you encircled this photograph, I couldn't quite follow why you decided that this is a place of an impact of a shrapnel. Can you explain that further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Certainly. If this is the footpath, this is the surface where this defect, this damage is located. On that surface, it's absolutely -- when the shell falls here and projects shrapnel normally, it's absolutely impossible for this damage in this place to occur at 90 degrees. Because all the damage, all the projection of shrapnel, goes into the area ahead or laterally. It cannot be found on a surface which is 90 degrees to that surface, to the other surface. We call that in artillery a dead angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I stop you. This is not what I asked you for. I wanted to know where we can see on this photograph that there is a damage caused by shrapnel. I don't see a damage there. On what observation did you base your claim that at this location there was a damage caused by a shrapnel? I don't see anything there. Did you use different information? Have you visited the site? Or what is it what you based your observation on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly we visited the location. And when we visited the location, this footpath had been repaved. You could not see it then. We used this photograph where you see this little defect in the shape of an arch that I marked here. If we looked even more carefully, if we could analyse this photograph even better, we would probably find other damage from shrapnel. This is the impact of a larger piece of shrapnel that is visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In my view, there's nothing visible which could indicate that there is a damage which is caused by shrapnel. I just don't see anything like that. And I wanted to ask you for assistance so that I can really -- from this photograph, take that there is a damage on the site of the footpath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just explained this. This is this little arch pointing downwards and it's on the side of this curb. I marked it -- the way I marked it looks like a smiley. This is the damage that is very clearly seen on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is your opinion. Thank you. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask you if you would look at it, I think it may be some rubble that is there. What makes you so sure that what you marked is, indeed, shrapnel traces rather than some rubble or whatever? From this photograph. And that's what we seek your assistance, to better -- you made an arc, but you can make an arc on rubble as well and ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a clear trace based on the rules of our profession. There are several other traces that indicate impact on the edge of the playground in the photo documentation these points of impact are marked. There is testimony to those points of impact. There are traces on the ground that could not have been created in any different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now you are explaining a lot of other things. What we are seeking is your assistance to establish clearly that this is not rubble but this is shrapnel impact. And testimonies, et cetera, you drew this conclusion on the basis of this photograph, and, therefore, we're seeking your assistance to be able to better understand how you could consider with certainty this to be shrapnel impacts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, you have here, right -- to the right, there is another trace of shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, for what you say now, we would again put the same question to you: What makes you so certain about what looks as dark and -- that that is shrapnel impact rather than anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you look at the upper photograph, you will see that wherever shrapnel hit on this footpath, all of these spots are dark, and we certainly know that the projectile did land above. Wherever there is violent deformation of the surface from shrapnel, all these spots are dark. You will see the same dark spots on the footpath above.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's mainly because it's dark that explains that it's shrapnel impact rather than any other matter that could appear to be dark, such as rubble sometimes is as well. Could have a dark colour as well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course it could be. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have one follow-up question. If this would be shrapnel impact, then apparently from another explosion, because you say it could not have been caused by this explosion. Did you find anything about an explosion within, well, let's say, a few metres from there which would have caused this shrapnel impact, as you consider it to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly. We analysed this explosion in great detail in this report. In photo documentation, it is marked as 1, and it is on the edge of the playground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please answer my question. Your claim is that what you marked in red is, first of all, shrapnel impact; second, not caused by the impact at number 1, if I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which raises the question as to what impact then caused this shrapnel traces which could not have been caused by explosion number 1. Did you find anything to explain that on those days or just before it or just after it, that another shell exploded at a very, very short distance from number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found that on that same day, there was an explosion on the edge of the playground, and this comes from that shell. There were also witnesses in this case who spoke about it. That's the fourth shell that they did not investigate. The investigators, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what was exactly the distance between the point of impact and this shrapnel trace -- these shrapnel traces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. I marked it the other day during examination. Let me just open that page so you can follow more easily too. Here it is. The picture, the still, taken from a video made by the investigators, figure 66. And figure 65. On both of them, one can see that it's very close, looking down that path, that is to say, along the playground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How close?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it can't be more than half a metre, looking down the path.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I now want to discuss with you incident G-5 on 12 July 1993. In paragraph 62G of your report, you state: "It is particularly striking that although investigator Hamdija Cavcic that the reports of the Bosnian police and UNPROFOR were made independently of each other, UNPROFOR's report lists the names of the members of the Bosnian investigation team present there, and it is clear that the reports used the same data probably given by the Bosnian investigators to UNPROFOR which means that these two -- that these were not two independent reports whose results match." Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 11231 for the witness. And if we could go to page 2. This is the UNPROFOR report of its investigation. Under the heading, "Crater Characteristics," it says: "Form of the spray shows the direction of 5100 mills (WWN)." That corresponds to 287 degrees; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That direction of fire corresponds to the west, north-west; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: North-west, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Nowhere in this report does it say that UNPROFOR, that their calculation of the direction of fire came from data provided by the CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't. We did not even put it in our report that they referenced it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 11231 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 11231 receives exhibit number P7555, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- I'm a bit puzzled by putting 287 degrees at north-west. It's slightly north of north-west? Yes, I -- because you said that "direction of fire corresponds to the west, north-west; correct?" So not to be understood as to the west of north-west but, rather, slightly to the north of north-west because it's more than 270 degrees which is west.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take that you do not disagree, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's fine. It's north, north-west, meaning that it is in the quadrant demarking north and west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I made a mistake, as a matter of fact. I made a mistake. 287 is slightly west of north-west rather than -- because north-west would be 315. Yes. I apologise for making this mistake and very kind of you, Ms. Subotic, to agree that it's in that quadrant demarking north and west which avoids to comment on my mistake. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have D01251. And if we could please go to English page 6 and B/C/S page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the portion of the investigative file containing the report of the on-site ballistics investigation by Mr. Cavcic. In the B/C/S version, toward the bottom of the page, which is about two-thirds of the way down in the English version, you see the conclusion that the: "Traces form an irregular arc direction north-west west." And then if we could please have page 11 of the B/C/S, the next page. I'm sorry, if we can go back one. There you go. Toward the end of the report, you see his conclusion regarding incoming direction of fire as north-west west. The fact is that the CSB assessment of direction of fire was done independently based on traces on the ground, not from data provided by someone else; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the CSB investigation team were on the scene, and they probably drafted this report we are looking at. It is just that it is quite unclear when someone writes that there are traces in the direction of west north-west not linking it to any particular photograph. I could simply say --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness kindly repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, I see that you're reading stuff back from your report. Could you please answer my question. That they independently --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do that. The interpreters asked the witness to repeat the last sentence. You said at a certain moment: "I could simply say," and could you repeat from what you then said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could simply say that it is not orientated whatsoever. Because if you put it that way, it could be placed in any which direction, not supported by any photographs or other evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to the CSB investigation on-site report that you have in front of you, they determined the direction of fire based on traces on the grounds. That's what we read here; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. However, the traces on the scene do not indicate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness, we'll soon take a break - not immediately - but you already may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I promised to prepare something for you over the break. I don't know whether you still want it and I would kindly ask the Prosecutor what it is that I had to prepare. There was a quote, I think?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A quote of ours that we managed to locate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was about the compass method used. And Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need to do it any further because we found it as well. Mr. Lukic was kindly assisting in pointing us at the relevant paragraph. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take a break, I'd like to briefly address a matter and do that before we continue with the examination of Witness Subotic. The Chamber would like to address some of the Defence's submissions made in court some two weeks ago. The key issue with respect to expert witnesses is the following: Expert witnesses should testify according to their field of expertise. Witness Zorica Subotic was presented, and I quote from the Defence notice of the 10th of April, 2015: "As ballistics, fire-arms and cold weapons expert." According to her CV, the witness has special identified knowledge in this field. The Chamber has not limited and will not limit a party in eliciting evidence from an expert witness, if this evidence falls within the scope of his or her expertise. This includes testimony about the facts the expert bases his or her report findings on. Such a facts may also be testimony of a witness of fact. However, in the view of the Chamber, it is inappropriate for an expert witness to evaluate the reliability and credibility of such fact witnesses or such a fact witness. It is for the Chamber to exercise this evaluation in view of the totality of the evidence before it. This is the background of the Chamber's efforts to support the parties and control the conduct of proceedings during the examination of witnesses. In this context, the Chamber refers the parties to Rule 90(F) of our Rules which provide the following: "The Trial Chamber shall exercise control over the mode and order of interrogating witnesses and presenting evidence so as to: (i) make the integration of witnesses and for the ascertainment of truth; and (ii) to avoid needless of consumption of time." The Chamber is aware that some of its interventions were understood in a different way. However, in the interests of a fair - and I stress - expeditious trial, we all should do our utmost best to adhere to these principles. This was the Chamber's short statement. We take a break and resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If at this time I could just make use of the moment to tender 65 ter 33095B, as in boy. It's a video-clip from the 1 hour, 59 minute, and 54 second mark through 2 hours, 1 minute, and 38 seconds of ERN V000-2479, which is the video referenced in relation to incident G-5 in footnote 225 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It hasn't been used so ... I don't know how could we check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's referenced by the expert. I'd like to go through the incident in an expeditious possible manner and we would just ask that the video that is referenced in the report be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if the expert witness relies on it, is there any reason why we should not have an opportunity to check that footnote by having it in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course not, Your Honour, only we have A here referenced before and ... 33095A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is exactly what I wanted to ask Mr. Weber: What is the difference between the A version and B version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Same video. It's a rather long video. There are multiple incidents depicted on it. With respect to the A version, that related to earlier incident and now in that same video we would like to tender the portion that relates to the incident at hand, which is incident G-5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the B version includes the A version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: These are two different parts of the same entire video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you excerpted various portions relate to the specific incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That video, as I understand it, was admitted under D1250.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you check that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was not admitted. It was marked for identification, but only the A version which was shown to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A is even -- no, I think that D1250 is the whole video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I believe that relates to incident G-4 and we'd like to admit the portion for G-5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would please verify that and then revisit the matter once it has been verified. Witness, apologies for dealing with all kind of administrative matters, although still related to your testimony. Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You testified at transcript page 39255 and wrote in your report at paragraphs 53 and 54 that there were military facilities nearby the site of the shelling on the 12th of July, 1993. First of all, could you please confirm that this assertion is not from your personal knowledge but, rather, based solely based on the statement of another witness in a different trial?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we referenced that in footnote 195. That's the testimony of Ismet Hadzic in the Galic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm a bit confused on your theory about the possible military facility and this incident. Is it your theory that the ABiH fired the shell on 12 July 1993 trying to target their own military command in Dobrinja or are you throwing this out there, just in the event that the Chamber agrees with the rest of the evidence that shows that it came from SRK territory. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of the two. Quite simply, we tried to put in all the information we had in order to have the most complete picture possible of the event, without any intention of showing that the BH army targeted themselves or create a route for retreat for ourselves. If -- because that kind of evidence, as you said yourself, does not pass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get clarification. When you say: "Create a route for retreat for ourselves." Who are the "ourselves" here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean myself and my colleague who co-authored the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what would you be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what would be you retreating from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not mean retreat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just tried to put all the facts in one place so that you, as the Trial Chamber, would have a complete insight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. You -- but said you didn't want to create a route for retreat for yourselves. What would you be retreating from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's a matter of interpretation. Because the theory of the Prosecution was that we had one of these two things in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. I'm just trying to understand your answer. I understood the Prosecution's question clearly, but I don't understand your answer why you say "create a route for retreat" for yourselves, referring to your and your co-author. I'm trying to find out what are you retreating from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say that we provided all the information that we had and that we believe were necessary to the Trial Chamber. We did not have the intention, either to say that the BH army targeted themselves, for whatever reason, or to create a backup position for ourselves in the sense that if our analysis is not accepted, to have a fallback position saying that it was, in fact, a military target. None of these things. We just wanted to the Trial Chamber to have a clear and complete insight into the situation on the ground when the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33202 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 12 July 1993 SRK Command order from General Galic to continue the execution of Operation Lukavac '93. This order is issued on the same day of the G-5 shelling. Directing your attention to the third paragraph which states: "In order to inflict on the enemy the biggest possible losses and prevent the consolidation of enemy units, which are in disarray, and prevent the hampering of the execution of further combat activities for liberating Serb Mount Igman and Serb villages at the foot of the Mount Bjelasnica and connecting Serb Trnovo with Ilidza and Hadzici via Mount Igman." Dobrinja sits in between Trnovo and Ilidza; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I put it to you that the shelling of the water distribution line in Dobrinja on 12 July was committed by the VRS and was part of ongoing operations at the time. This is what happened; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not. The material evidence on the ground shows that it is not correct. We analysed that in detail. If you want us to go through that evidence step by step, we can. But to take such a general view just because of that order, we cannot do that. Because of the evidence on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 33202 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33202 receives exhibit number P7556, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Turning to the shelling of the water distribution point on 18 June 1995, you discuss this between pages 166 and 184 of your shelling report. You do not reference any UN materials for this incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You realise that Enes Turkusic, as he has testified both in this case and in the past Karadzic case, did not determine the direction of fire in this incident from the sketch, which you discuss; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he stated that he had determined the direction of fire by method of elimination. That's one. And, two, the traces at the point of impact. Through a procedure of elimination, which he did not explain during his evidence in Karadzic when we asked him to explain that to us, he said he couldn't do it without his sketch, and if you or your colleagues had been able to supply him with that sketch, maybe he could have explained it better.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution doesn't agree with you but I'm not going to dwell on it because the Chamber has the evidence. I'm going to move on and discuss the incident in Bascarsija on 22nd December 1994. For this incident, you reviewed the investigative file from the Bosnian MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The old town area of Sarajevo contains many stores where many of the city's residents shop; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I suppose they did their shopping back then, too. There are many shops there, although in war time, God knows how much was available to buy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's not clear so I'm asking you directly here, do you believe that there were two explosions on this date? One or two?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly two explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that is not contested.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were aware from your review of the investigative materials that shell fragments from two M70 76-millimetre shells were found at the scene; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 76-millimetre M70. Parts of shells that were found belonged to a 76-millimetre projectile of the type M70, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is not uncommon to find a fuse from a projectile at or near the location of a mortar or artillery explosion. You know this; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's rather unusual for it to be found complete. If it was the fuse that caused the explosion, one should follow through the whole process. The fuse was the one that initiated the explosion. So it is the first thing that falls apart into fragments. It does not remain on the spot, whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. The Chamber has heard evidence about that. We're not in agreement about it. I'd like to address the issues raised in your report regarding the first explosion at Danila Ilica Street. In paragraph 103 of your report, you suggest that the scene of the incident was altered substantially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. We just heard that the Chamber has heard the evidence that after the explosion of mortar or grenade shell, it is common to have whole fuse. That's what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, then, can you explain, please what this Chamber heard, what was your intention. Page 70, line 6, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was attempting to address was in what we -- it's not agreement, just to be specific, is the condition of the fuse that was recovered at the scene which I believe the Chamber has heard evidence about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You believe or you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic -- I'm coming to it, Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I would like to have that quotation then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well now. It was a marginal observation about what would be in evidence or not, and I think, as a matter of fact, that you didn't want to put that to the witness in any way. So, therefore, I can imagine that you would like to know, Mr. Lukic, and Mr. Weber will certainly tell you what you thinks about it during the next break. Meanwhile, it is not part of the examination of the witness and just a marginal observation; right or wrong. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 103 of your report, you suggest that the scene of this incident was altered substantially, and this was relating to the first explosion. Your theory is that the scene of the first explosion was altered by the polices in the course of the on-site investigation, including by digging up a crater manually in the asphalt and covering marks designed to look like shrapnel in metal shutters during the two hours and 40 minutes when the investigators were on the scene. Have I stated your theory correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the things you said are correct; others are not. It is correct that we stated the scene was altered. It is true that we said the earth was moved, and that is visible; but it is not correct that we said that they covered anything up. It's not in my text. If you read it carefully, you will see that. Each alteration that we noticed is marked with numbers and is very easy to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If there was an explosion, the police would not have needed to carve markings to look like shrapnel because there would have been shrapnel from the explosion; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The police would not have needed to dig a crater if there was an explosion because there would be a crater; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm -- if you are talking about the -- an explosion created by a projectile, not any type of explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You understood me correctly. In your report, one reason you come to the conclusion that the scene was altered is that the crater is too big for a 76-millimetre artillery round and I'm referring to -- to -- for example, page 148 of your report. It appears that you explain that -- or you analogise the fact that such an artillery round has a similar explosive charge as an 82-millimetre mortar. First, do you base this on photographs from the MUP file, this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did not have any other photographs. We only had the MUP photo documentation. And it's true that this M70 76-millimetre projectile is similar to an 82-millimetre shell in terms of explosive mass. It has -- one has 600 and the other has 680 grams. So it's -- one has an explosive mass of 15 per cent higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your view, do mortars and artillery shells cause similar or different patterns on the ground upon impact?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They always leave different traces upon impact, but the size of the crater is primarily defined by the mass of the explosive charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A mortar shell of a similar calibre as an artillery shell, I put it to you, produces more shrapnel, less of a blast effect and a different pattern based upon the rotation or non-rotation of the shell during its flight; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, a shell, an artillery shell, certainly rotates during flight because of system of stabilisation is stabilisation through rotation. These are stable projectiles. And, second, a mortar projectile rotates only slightly and its rotation is much smaller than that of an artillery projectile. I don't know exactly what you were driving at with this question. If you -- if you make it clearer, maybe I can answer more precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In simplest terms, what I'm putting to you is that you're comparing apples and oranges, because there is more shrapnel, less of a blast effect, and a different pattern between a mortar shell of a similar calibre as a given artillery shell?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you that I am comparing apples and oranges. The number of pieces of shrapnel depends on a number of factors which is probably beyond the scope of our discussion here. You cannot say in a blanket fashion that there are more shrapnel with a mortar shell. It depends on far greater number of parameters than we can discuss here now. Secondly, I suppose that a mine shell, having 15 per cent more of explosive should create at least this kind of crater, if not greater. Another thing that we disagree on is the trace left on a surface. It is different when it comes to an artillery projectile as opposed to a mortar projectile. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. In addition, the size -- well, you cite the damage to the shutter shown in the photo file as a reason you believe the site may have been altered. You claim that, and I quote from paragraph 105 of your report: "It is impossible for so much shrapnel to hit the window without any of it hitting the wall." When making this conclusion you also refer to the testimony of Ekrem Suljevic and state in the same paragraph that Mr. Suljevic: "Did not explicitly state why the damage to the wall was not marked in circles on these photographs." I'd like to now turn to Mr. Suljevic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33156. And if we could scroll down to about line 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the testimony of Ekrem Suljevic in the Karadzic case on 6 September 2010, page 6203, the same portion that you reference in footnote 417. Starting at line 21, during this testimony, Mr. Suljevic was asked: "Q. How do you explain that will are some markings on the shutter, most probably marked by chalk, whereas we see now no damages inflicted by fragments on the wall? "A. I wouldn't dare claim that, based on this photograph. If we were to examine it more carefully, we may be able to find some damages, but they aren't marked. But the narrative under the photograph says that the purpose of this photograph was to show the damage done to the metal shutter." Were you present when Mr. Suljevic gave this explanation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Mr. Suljevic provided his explanation as recorded. However, the gist of the problem is that underneath the photograph in the photo file there's no reference made to any wall marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... ma'am, we have the answer. You did not quote or mention Mr. Suljevic's non-agreement with the proposition that the photograph shows no damages on the wall or his explanation to Mr. Karadzic of the purpose of the photograph being to show damage on the shutter; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember him saying that, but not as explicitly as it is recorded here. At least not as far as I remember. In any case, it is illogical and I know how such records are made. It is illogical that somebody would write something that is incorrect underneath a photograph. There is no situation in which --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you're explaining. I'm just putting to you you're not accurately reflecting the evidence of the witness in your report. We see another occasion of that; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's your opinion, then let it lie. But I don't think we inaccurately presented the witness's statement. I disagree with that. I was present during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your report at paragraph 98 you note that UNPROFOR members from the 4th French Battalion and UNMOs from the SC2 group stationed at Sedrenik were at the scene of the shelling on the -- in December 1994. Do you really believe that investigators managed to conceal the fact that they had altered a scene, including by manually excavating a crater in the asphalt and carving marks to look like shrapnel and metal shutters from seven UN officials who were on the scene at the time? Do you expect us to really believe that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not in a position to believe or disbelieve. I wasn't present. I look at technical evidence, so to say, as a consequence of the physical forces. I analyse those. If you can't accept that, I don't know how to continue this conversation with you. Whether I believe in something or not has no place in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The UN investigators analysed the craters and, like the police, they concluded that the shells were -- well, that the craters were the result of shells fired from the south-east; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's talk about the second explosion at number 3 Petra Kocica Street. In relation to the second explosion you claim in paragraph 107 of your report that the round at the second site was activated while it was stationary. Are you saying that this was a staged static explosion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I did not say that it was elevated but placed flat because the crater as we have it in figure 98 taken over from the photo file --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or the recording taken --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't know if it was recorded correctly. I meant to say that it was activated while it was stationary not elevated. Are you saying that this was a staged static explosion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no other choice but to state that given the technical parameters in the field and the traces, material traces that we examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You cannot give me a name of any witness or individual who saw this explosive device planted; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. But, really, based on what could I provide you with such a name?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33162 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you are the technical specifications for a --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if I could please actually go forward. I'm sorry. If we could go to the second page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you are the technical specifications for a 76-millimetre artillery round from the ammunition manual. Based upon these specifications, a 76-millimetre artillery round is 64 centimetres long and weighs over 8 kilograms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These specifications are quite different from an 82-millimetre shell. Here, the entire 76-millimetre shell weighs 8.2 kilos of which it appears 5.2 kilograms is the steel jacket. Whereas as we discussed earlier, I believe, the 82-millimetre shell, the entire round weighs just over 3 kilograms. The steel jacket of a 76-millimetre shell is significantly higher and thicker than an 82-millimetre mortar shell; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. But let me correct interpretation. I heard the interpreter twice say full jacket, but it is actually the round that the weight referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you may ask a question about interpretation. You are not here to correct the interpretation. If you have any concerns in that respect, then we'll verify it. Because our interpreters are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- are experts in their field. Therefore, you, as a layperson may, again, express any concerns, but it will always be verified and will be dealt with at the level of expert knowledge for interpretation. Mr. Lukic, if there are any concerns, then the -- you -- the witness said -- let me just ... one second, please. You said that you heard twice the word "full jacket." It doesn't not appear on the transcript in English, and I don't remember that I've heard --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: She's listening to B/C/S channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But in the B/C/S channel, I think there would be no -- or is that the words of Mr. Weber were not accurately translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then if that's the case, please point at which concerns you may have and then it will be verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The question could just be restated. But I see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check one second, please. If there are any concerns in this respect --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 77, from line 14 could be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 77, line 14. Mr. Weber, that is -- I have on 77, line 14: "These specifications are quite different from an 82-millimetre shell. Here, the entire 76-millimetre shell weighs 8.2 kilos of which appears 5.2 kilograms is the steel jacket. Whereas we discussed earlier, I believe, the 82-millimetre shell, the entire round weighs just over 3 kilograms." Any concerns left, Mr. Lukic? Mr. Weber, I -- The witness raised the matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The -- let the translator to translate this time all the way through. I don't know if there's any concerns now at Ms. Subotic's side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If any concern remains, Mr. Lukic, then we'd have to compare the previous translation of the same words spoken by Mr. Weber and the -- the interpretation and now the interpretation of my words when I literally read from the transcript what Mr. Weber is supposed to have said. If there's any concern, we'll hear from you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could tender 65 ter 33162 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33162 receives exhibit number P7557, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7557 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just quickly completing for the day Mr. Lukic inquired about Mr. Suljevic's testimony regarding the fuse. I would refer counsel to transcript page 8533 of these proceedings and the discussion in that page. And I see that it's the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It certainly is. Ms. Subotic, I give you the same instructions as I did before, that is, not to speak or communicate in whatever way about your testimony with whomever, whether already given or still to be given. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 6th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
